title: An ample limit fibre gives an ample affine neighbourhood at a Noetherian stage
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set with least element $0$. Let $(f_i:Y_i\to X_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with affine transition morphisms $q_{ji}:Y_j\to Y_i$ and $r_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism] satisfying $f_iq_{ji}=r_{ji}f_j$. Assume every $X_i$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Let $Y$ and $X$ be the respective limits with projections $a_i,b_i$ and induced morphism $f:Y\to X$, so $f_i a_i=b_i f$; a limit here means that each compatible cone from any scheme factors uniquely through the given projections. Let $M_0$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_{Y_0}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], put $M_i=q_{i0}^*M_0$, and let $M$ be an invertible module on $Y$ with $a_0^*M_0\cong M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $x\in X$ put $x_i=b_i(x)$ and let $Y_x,(Y_i)_{x_i}$ denote scheme-theoretic fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $M|_{Y_x}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], then there exist $i\in I$ and an affine open neighbourhood $V_i\subseteq X_i$ of $x_i$ such that both $M_i|_{(Y_i)_{x_i}}$ and $M_i|_{f_i^{-1}(V_i)}$ are ample in the absolute sense.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, proof: residue-field colimit, descent of fibre ampleness, and the Noetherian affine neighbourhood V_i.

proof.text: Put $k_i=\kappa(x_i)$ and $P_i=\operatorname{Spec}k_i$. The residue-field limit theorem applied to $(X_i)$ and $x$ gives the compatible cone $P=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)=\varprojlim_iP_i$, including its compatibility with $P_i\to X_i$. Put $Z_i=Y_i\times_{X_i}P_i$. The transition $t_{ji}:Z_j\to Z_i$ is induced by $q_{ji}$ and $P_j\to P_i$; the fibre-product uniqueness gives its identity and composition laws.

source.place: Tag 0CUG, lemma-inverse-limit-irreducibles (1); construction of the fibre system

proof.text: Each $Z_i\to P_i$ is proper by base change of $f_i$. Since $P_i$ is affine, proper-basic gives that $Z_i$ is quasi-compact and separated; the separated-implies-quasi-separated lemma gives quasi-separatedness of $Z_i$. Thus these are schemes to which affine-limit ampleness descent can apply once the transitions have been checked.

source.place: Tag 01W6, lemma-base-change-proper; proper fibres over fields are quasi-compact and separated

proof.text: Fix $j\ge i$. Choose an affine open $V\subset X_i$ containing $x_i$, and cover $f_i^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $U_\alpha$. The open $V_j=r_{ji}^{-1}(V)$ and the opens $U_{j,\alpha}=q_{ji}^{-1}(U_\alpha)$ are affine by the hypotheses. Write $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)$, $B_\alpha=\Gamma(U_\alpha,\mathcal O)$, $A_j=\Gamma(V_j,\mathcal O)$ and $B_{j,\alpha}=\Gamma(U_{j,\alpha},\mathcal O)$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies the opens $U_\alpha\times_VP_i$ of $Z_i$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(B_\alpha\otimes_Ak_i)$, and their inverse images under $t_{ji}$ with $U_{j,\alpha}\times_{V_j}P_j=\operatorname{Spec}(B_{j,\alpha}\otimes_{A_j}k_j)$. These identifications follow by matching the two projections in the fibre-product universal property. The former opens cover $Z_i$ and every displayed inverse image is affine. The affine-local-target criterion therefore says that $t_{ji}$ is affine. No square $Y_j\to Y_i$ over $X_j\to X_i$ is assumed Cartesian.

source.place: Tags 01S6 and 01S8; schemes.tex Tag 01I4 (affine fibre products); direct chart verification of the fibre transitions

proof.text: The affine-transition limit theorem now ensures that $\varprojlim_i Z_i$ exists. Apply the fibre-products-and-limits theorem to the compatible systems $Y_i\to X_i\leftarrow P_i$. Their limits are $Y$, $X$ and $P$ by hypothesis and Step 1; it identifies $\varprojlim_iZ_i$ with $Y\times_XP=Y_x$, compatibly with all projections. This checks the limit required for ampleness descent without replacing a stage fibre by a base change of $Y_0$.

source.place: Tags 01YX and 0CUG; fibre-product universal property (commutation of limits)

proof.text: Let $p_i:Z_i\to Y_i$ be the first projection and put $L_0=p_0^*M_0$. Pullback preserves invertibility. The equality $q_{i0}p_i=p_0t_{i0}$ and the composition isomorphisms for tensor pullback give $t_{i0}^*L_0\cong p_i^*q_{i0}^*M_0=M_i|_{Z_i}$. Likewise its pullback to the limit $Y_x$ is $M|_{Y_x}$, using $a_0^*M_0\cong M$. This limit pullback is ample by assumption. Apply affine-limit ampleness descent to $(Z_i)$, whose quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are Step 2, affine transitions Step 3 and limit Step 4. It gives $i\ge0$ such that $M_i|_{Z_i}$ is ample.

source.place: Tag 09MT, lemma-limit-ample, applied to the fibre system; pullback-composition identifications

proof.text: The pullback $M_i=q_{i0}^*M_0$ is invertible. Apply the Noetherian fibre-ampleness neighbourhood lemma to the original proper morphism $f_i:Y_i\to X_i$, this invertible module, and $x_i$. Its base is Noetherian by hypothesis and its fibre restriction is ample by Step 5. It gives an affine open $V_i$ containing $x_i$ on whose full inverse image $M_i$ is absolutely ample. Together with the fibre ampleness already obtained, this is both conclusions of the item. No further change of index is necessary.

source.place: Tag 0D2N, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood; restriction to an affine neighbourhood

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q87-fb8c936a3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks Tag 0D2S (more-morphisms.tex lines 14153-14198). The item is the middle paragraph of its proof: residue fields κ(y)=colim κ(y_i), then 09MT on the fibres, then 0D2N, with the Noetherian approximation taken as hypotheses. The statement is unchanged; live and side-live still have it unsplit with an empty proof, so no other group has superseded it. There is no re-split note and there are no new nodes. proof_deps equals the union of uses. No SGA is cited. Step checks: (1) lem-weil-pbc-limit-residue-field gives P=lim P_i compatibly with P_i→X_i and P→X; the fibre system Z_i=Y_i×_{X_i}P_i is well defined because f_i q_ji=r_ji f_j. (2) Proper base change, then pqf-lem-proper-basic's affine-base clause, then separated⇒quasi-separated make each Z_i qcqs. (3) I checked the charts: t_ji^{-1}(p_i^{-1}U_α)=U_{j,α}×_{V_j}P_j, which is affine by affineness of q and r and the affine fibre-product node; the affine-local-target criterion then makes t_ji affine with no Cartesian assumption. (4) The limit of the Z_i exists because the transitions are affine; lem-kun-fibre-product-limits, with all limits existing, identifies it with Y×_X P=Y_x. (5) The pullback composition identifications hold; lem-trf-ample-affine-limit-descent then makes M_i|_{Z_i} ample. (6) lem-trf-noetherian-fibre-ample-neighbourhood applied to f_i, M_i and x_i gives an affine V_i with absolute ampleness, at the same index i. Edge cases: I={0} reduces to 0D2N; an empty fibre is vacuous. I accept the 8 declared generic tool_uses. Duplicate search over 0D2S, 09MT and the ample-neighbourhood nodes found only the parent, the two siblings, the affine-square transfer node and the algebraic-space locus node, so the item is no duplicate and restates no parent clause. Advisory only: invariance of ampleness under isomorphism (the node lem-sc-ample-iso) is used implicitly in steps 5 and 6; I treat it as definition-level, so there is no change.
